audit.evidence: Real published npm dset 2.0.1/3.1.2/3.1.4 installed side-by-side via npm aliases; minimal HTTP harness GET /probe drives the real dset() bytes; observed original pollution flag@v0 blocked@v1, residual flag@v1 blocked@v2 (orig+residual blocked@v2), passed:true.

app_purpose: Tiny JavaScript deep-set utility library (npm `dset`, by lukeed); `dset(obj, keys, val)` splits/walks a dotted or array key path, creating intermediate objects/arrays, and assigns the leaf value (a nested set-by-path).
root_cause_note: CWE-1321 prototype pollution in dset()'s key-loop. The path walk dereferences each segment with `t = t[k]` (creating a namespace when absent), so a crafted segment `__proto__` (or `constructor`/`prototype`) makes the walk step OUT of the fresh target and ONTO a shared built-in prototype (Object.prototype), and the leaf write then ADDS/modifies a property on it. The pollution is GLOBAL (it mutates the real shared Object.prototype), so the harness restores (deletes) the injected property after each probe. The incomplete fix is a string-only key guard bypassed by a NON-string (array) key of the dangerous name = CWE-843 type confusion (CVE-2024-21529).
source_verified_caveat: SOURCE-LEVEL NUANCE (verified against the real git repo lukeed/dset and the real npm tarballs, not just aggregator metadata): the string-comparison guard in the CORE dset() (src/index.js) `if (k === '__proto__' || k === 'constructor' || k === 'prototype') break;` was first introduced in dset 3.0.0 (commit 0a11c8a 'fix: break loop on unsafe keys', 2021-01-27), NOT by CVE-2022-25645's 3.1.2 release. CVE-2022-25645's 3.1.2 fix (commit 2d156c7) added a SIBLING guard to the separate `dset/merge` helper's `for (k in b)` copy loop (src/merge.js). dset@3.1.1/3.1.2/3.1.3 all carry the byte-identical string-only dset() guard; dset@3.1.4 (CVE-2024-21529 fix, commit 16d6154) adds `k = ''+keys[i++]` string coercion. This case models the incomplete-fix at the CORE dset() sink (the sink CVE-2024-21529 fixes): the string-only key guard vs the string-coerced guard, with the array-key residual as the exact CVE-2024-21529 bypass. V0 is pinned to dset@2.0.1, the last published version whose dset() has NO key guard at all, so the plain-string `__proto__` seed genuinely pollutes on V0 and is genuinely blocked on V1 (a real differential on the same sink). The plain-string seed represents the CVE-2022-25645-class prototype pollution (a `__proto__` path segment reaching Object.prototype through dset); it is NOT claimed to be byte-for-byte CVE-2022-25645's `dset/merge` PoC.

flag.resource: default-deny authorization gate (`Object.prototype.pcbUnlock` is ABSENT, re-ensured absent before/after each probe) that DENIES by default; releases the planted secret only if the crafted dset() call ADDED a truthy `pcbUnlock` onto Object.prototype (prototype pollution by addition)

sink: dset src/index.js — the dset() key-loop guard on path segments. The walk dereferences each segment with `t = t[k]`; a `__proto__` (or `constructor`/`prototype`) segment, as a STRING (seed) or as a NON-string array element (residual), makes the leaf write land on Object.prototype.
residual: The string-comparison guard (V1 = dset@3.1.2) compares the RAW key with strict `===` against the STRINGS '__proto__'/'constructor'/'prototype' (`k = keys[i++]`, no coercion). A path whose segment is itself an array — `[['__proto__'],'pcbUnlock']` — makes the dangerous key the array `['__proto__']`; `['__proto__'] === '__proto__'` is FALSE so the guard passes it, then `t[k]` coerces the array to the string '__proto__' and the walk steps onto Object.prototype = CVE-2024-21529. The string `['__proto__','pcbUnlock']` seed is blocked on V1; the array-key residual is not.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2024-21529: dset before 3.1.4 is vulnerable to prototype pollution via the dset function; a malicious `__proto__` property (supplied as a non-string / array key that the string-only guard does not catch) is assigned onto Object.prototype. Framed by Snyk as a residual of the earlier `__proto__` sanitization; the 3.1.4 patch coerces keys to strings before the guard check.

notes: node:20-slim faithful-core; REAL published dset bytes per version via npm aliases (2.0.1/3.1.2/3.1.4); the harness drives the REAL dset(). Same-sink Variant A incomplete-fix at the CORE dset() key-loop: V1 (dset@3.1.2) guards keys with a strict `===` STRING comparison and no coercion (`k = keys[i++]`); the residual `[['__proto__'],'pcbUnlock']` reaches Object.prototype because the array key is `!== '__proto__'` yet coerces back to '__proto__' when used as `t[k]` (CWE-843 type confusion); V2 (dset@3.1.4) coerces `k = ''+keys[i++]` first and blocks it. V0 (dset@2.0.1) has NO dset() guard so the plain-string `['__proto__','pcbUnlock']` seed pollutes and is genuinely blocked on V1. Benign canary: prototype pollution BY ADDITION flips a default-deny gate (Object.prototype.pcbUnlock absent => denied) releasing a planted PCB_FLAG; benign own-property writes never trip it. Pollution is GLOBAL (real Object.prototype), restored per probe to keep probes isolated. See source_verified_caveat: the dset() string guard originated in 3.0.0, not CVE-2022-25645's 3.1.2 (which patched the sibling dset/merge helper); this case models the incomplete-fix at the dset() sink that CVE-2024-21529 actually fixes.
